title: Principal Product Designer
description:
We are a global team of innovators and pioneers dedicated to shaping the future of observability. At New Relic, we build an intelligent platform that empowers companies to thrive in an AI\-first world by giving them unparalleled insight into their complex systems. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we're looking for passionate people to join our mission. If you're ready to help the world's best companies optimize their digital applications, we invite you to explore a career with us!

**Your opportunity**

  


As a Principal Product Designer on the UX Platform team, you will be the most senior individual design voice across the breadth of the UX Platform: the products our engineers and customers rely on every day, and the Design System that ties them together. You will partner closely with our Design Director as a trusted right hand, owning the hardest and most ambiguous problems, setting the quality bar, and helping decisions move so design is never the bottleneck.



Two things sit at the center of this role: designing for AI\-native experiences, and rethinking how design itself gets done in AI\-first workflows. We are fully immersed in both, and this role has a real hand in shaping where they go. We want someone genuinely eager to learn, test, and experiment here, but with the judgment to tell where AI raises the quality of the work and where it just adds noise. The aim is to use AI where it genuinely makes the work better, not to adopt it for its own sake.



You are a pragmatic optimist: ambitious about where we could go, honest about the terrain in front of us. You can hold “this is hard and might not work” and “let’s do it anyway, here’s how” in the same breath. You lead through craft and influence rather than authority, you take a vague problem and give it shape, you bring strong opinions but invite better ones, and you raise risks early and honestly. You lift the people around you by example, and the whole team’s work gets sharper because you are on it.

  


**What you'll do**

  

* Own the most complex and ambiguous design problems across our platform scope, from framing through detailed craft, end to end and with no oversight required.
* Design for AI\-native experiences: shape interfaces that are non\-deterministic and adapt to each use, design for outputs we cannot fully predict, and set the design principles and heuristics that keep those experiences coherent.
* Evolve how we design in AI\-first, spec\-driven workflows: help define how our role shifts, act as a multiplier for the team, and build ways to evaluate that we are shipping higher quality software, not just more of it.
* Set the bar for documentation and traceability: clear specs, references, and rationale that the team, our partners, and our AI tools can build on.
* Act as a second senior point of design judgment and a subject matter expert on our product: deputize for the Design Director in Product and Engineering reviews, shape strategic direction, and hold the quality bar across the whole product, not only your own area.
* Strengthen the connection between product design and the Design System, and define systems and processes that others across the company can benefit from.
* Partner with Product and Engineering to align on direction and keep work moving at a healthy cadence.
* Mentor designers, lead by example, and raise the overall level of craft across the team.


**This role requires**

  

* Extensive product design experience, including senior or lead work on complex software products.
* A portfolio that shows depth of craft and systems thinking across both product design and design systems, and recognized mastery of craft: a track record of raising the collective quality bar and defining patterns, systems, or processes that others adopt.
* A track record of owning ambiguous problems independently and driving them to real outcomes, end to end and without oversight.
* Comfort designing for AI\-native, non\-deterministic experiences, and enthusiasm for evolving how design gets done in AI\-first workflows.
* A discerning approach to AI: eager to experiment, but with the judgment to tell where it adds real value, and a quality bar that does not bend for the sake of hype.
* Ability to act as a subject matter expert who shapes priorities, leads research where useful, and interprets analysis into design decisions.
* Proven ability to influence Product and Engineering partners without formal authority.
* Excellent written and verbal communication in English, and a habit of documenting decisions, rationale, and references clearly so that people and tools can build on them.


**Bonus points if you have**


* Experience designing services and platforms, especially in observability, developer tools, data, or complex B2B products.
* A technical background: an understanding of modern software architecture, and experience with data visualization.
* Experience contributing to or stewarding a design system at scale.
* Hands\-on experience with spec\-driven or AI\-assisted design workflows.
* Comfort working in a distributed, cross\-cultural team.


Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

* **Experience:** Minimum of 5 years of senior sourcing experience, specifically focused on **Electronic Components and** **assemblies.**

* A fast\-growing company with real momentum
* A creative, international team based in Barcelona

title: Electrical Project Manager
description:
Mercury is the European leader in construction solutions.



We build and manage complex engineering \& construction projects for the world’s leading corporations. Our solutions help deliver technologies and life changing advancements that connect people, communities, and businesses, giving them the power to achieve incredible things. Our people have the courage to be innovative. Their determination and sharp focus enable us to deliver with certainty, time and time again.



We deliver our clients’ visions through leading edge construction solutions across multiple sectors, including Enterprise Data Centres, Advanced Technology \& Life Sciences, Hyperscale Data Centres, Fire Protection.



At Mercury, it is our duty to encourage and back our people to realise their vision of themselves. We place them at the heart of what we do, providing challenging opportunities to develop within a great team in a supportive environment that allows them to reach their full potential.

  


**Key Responsibilities of the Role:**


* Management of the Electrical Systems package and leadership of all electrical construction activities on site.
* Management of the OFCI / Main Capital electrical equipment and packages.
* Management of all day\-to\-day site operations relating to the electrical scope and interfaces with other trades.
* Ensure Mercury policies and procedures are followed closely.
* Familiarisation with Design/IFC specifications and drawings to fully understand the scope of the project works.
* Management of Site Safety in conjunction with the Project Manager and the Mercury Safety Advisor, including the setup, management and closing out of the safety file as part of the Management team.
* Ensure all work activities are planned to the required level of detail, with all documentation in line with company SOPs (RAMS, SPAs, Permits) and approved at the workface.
* Ensure all work is delivered in accordance with the permitting requirements of Mercury's Electrical Safety Rules and all applicable Safe Systems of Work.
* Ensure compliance with COHE and the Operating \& Energisation Procedures for LV \& MV systems, including arc flash awareness and controls.
* Oversee the room permits process and ensure contractors on site are compliant with requirements.
* Drive a focused Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QEHS) culture within your team and subcontractors, and drive the Mercury Engineering culture of safety and quality through the project.
* Ensure all EHS alerts are communicated effectively and understood by the team, and engage in campaigns including TBTs, stand\-downs, demonstrations and safety initiatives.
* Issue weekly safety stats and project labour projections.
* Management of Site QA in conjunction with the Mercury QA Manager, including set up, management and close out of the QA file, and review of contractor QAQC documentation and site performance.
* Ensure works are installed in accordance with project specifications and to the Project QA plan (e.g. pre\-agreed benchmarking).
* Review drawings and setting\-out details.
* Review quality of output and foster a culture of continuous improvement, implementing corrective actions where required.
* Manage and oversee the quality inspection regime, ensuring subcontractors carry out and maintain all quality inspections, ITPs, RFTs and snag closure as part of their scope, and hold them accountable for completing and submitting these on time and in line with the Project QA plan.
* Management of the electrical design process in conjunction with the Design Manager.
* Oversee the coordination process to transform design information into full installation drawings via BIM personnel, ensuring spec compliance and schedule priority.
* Manage the generation and close\-out of RFIs and technical queries, value engineering initiatives and design risk management.
* Management of the Project Schedule in conjunction with the Mercury Project Manager, Planner, consulting Engineer and Client requirements, including weekly progress updates.
* Ensure all site works are planned according to site production control requirements (Visilean or other collaborative planning).
* Drive digital collaborative planning and Lean construction processes to ensure effective coordination, efficient execution of works and timely delivery of milestones.
* Use project lookaheads to drive delivery and resource planning.
* Schedule material deliveries to correspond with the project schedule and track all deliveries.
* Management of all costs associated with your package including: Mercury Electrical Team; Sub\-contractors; Material deliveries and goods receipting; Plant and Equipment; Variations; Valuations.
* Own the commercial performance of the package, ensuring timely identification, management and recovery of variations, claims and commercial risks.
* Ensure subcontractor invoicing is measured in accordance with agreed progress milestones.
* Ensure Material Take\-Offs (MTOs) are completed and reviewed against subcontractor pricing returns and procurement budgets.
* Prepare Sub\-contract and Supplier Tender Packages in conjunction with the Project QS.
* Ensure subcontractors used have been vetted and approved by Mercury Procurement before use.
* Issue weekly cost reports, including all orders placed, materials expected and labour levels.
* Management of sub\-contractor activities including tracking progress against schedule and manpower levels. Ensure there is a weekly minuted meeting with sub\-contractors.
* Monitor that subcontractors have sufficiently resourced the project to maintain programme delivery.
* Management of the Mercury "In Progress" snagging system, ensuring supervisors return weekly punch lists where applicable, and ensure all snags are distributed to and closed out by all sub\-contractors.
* Maintain an active risk register and implement mitigation measures, highlighting any risk elements within Mercury's control (e.g. late deliveries).
* Implement the Mercury Project Audit Plan, review weekly audits and address open items with your team.
* Drive closure of all open audit actions within agreed timelines and communicate findings clearly to all stakeholders.
* Capture and act on lessons learned.
* Issue direct labour hours and sub\-contractor hours to the time administrator for tracking centrally.
* Issue an internal weekly progress report rolled up from project supervisors' reports, highlighting percentage complete based on WBS codes and any concerns or risks within Mercury's control.
* Issue an external weekly progress report to the Project Manager, highlighting areas not available, delays, shortage of design, third\-party hold\-ups and percentage complete.
* Attendance at Site Meetings, Internal Project Reviews, Engineering Reviews, Planning and Co\-ordination Meetings and Handover Meetings.
* Attend morning whiteboard meetings and evening planning/schedule review meetings.
* Maintain a weekly project photographic diary.
* Support and coach all the electrical team to ensure their development, which is crucial to our organisation and industry, supporting succession planning and team development.
* Set training requirements for Mercury and subcontractor staff and ensure appropriate training is available and completed.
* Direct management of the Mercury Engineering project team, including alignment of all discipline leads to the benefit of project goals.
* Drive the commissioning of all electrical equipment, taking ownership of completing the Red Tag (L2A – Installation) and Yellow Tag (L2B – Ready for Energisation) with all checklists and test documentation uploaded and approved in CxDE, then support the final commissioning levels — L3 Start\-Up (Green Tag), L4 Functional Performance Testing and Integrated System Testing (IST) — ensuring the electrical team and subcontractors deliver each level on time, to the required quality, and to CxA sign\-off.
* Close out of all project items including Final Account, O \& M Manuals, Punch List, Safety File, QA File, Material and Plant re\-locations and Project Plan – all with the support of the site Project Manager and your project team.
* All other duties associated with the role.

  


**Essential Criteria for the Role:**

* Overall 10\-15\+ years of experience in the construction sector.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Electrical, construction management, or other relevant degree.
* Minimum 5 years previous experience in Project Management
* Proven record of coordinating and managing large installation projects
* Experience dealing with Industrial Relations issues
* Knowledge of Health \& Safety
* Experienced in design and build
* Good technical knowledge of both Electrical and Mechanical systems
* Excellent IT skills
* Excellent communication skills
* Ability to work well within strict deadlines
* Ability to drive a large\-scale project

  


***Mercury is an equal opportunities employer*****.**

title: ITSM & Vendor Management Specialist
description:
Job Description:
* We are your **Energy Technology Partner**. We electrify, automate, and digitalize every industry, business, and home, driving efficiency and sustainability for all.

  

At Schneider Electric, our values – IMPACT (Inclusion, Mastery, Purpose, Action, Curiosity, Teamwork) – are the foundation of everything we do. Becoming an Impact Maker means turning sustainability ambitions into actions at the intersection of automation, electrification, and digitization.

  

Are you ready to lead the digital transformation to create a more sustainable world?


If you are up to challenge your creativity and make an impact, we are excited to welcome you!

 **Schneider Digital** is the digital department of Schneider Electric, leading the digital transformation in the company by giving support globally to our internal teams and our clients. Schneider Digital consists of 6 Digital Hubs worldwide which are strategically located to ensure a 24/7 support across the company (France, China, India, USA, Mexico and Spain). Our Digital Hub in Barcelona is formed by \+450 employees working in strategic projects and different roles such as Data, Cybersecurity, ERP, Cloud, Infrastructures, IT Project Management or Digital Marketing.

  

Schneider Electric is a Fortune 500 global enterprise operating a product\-oriented infrastructure model structured around technical pillars (Network, Compute \& Storage, Cloud, Automation, Monitoring) and supported by a broad ecosystem of strategic vendors. This model enables specialization and execution at scale, but also creates fragmentation risks across prioritization, standards, financial control, vendor management, and service performance.

Glovo is part of the Delivery Hero Group, the world’s pioneering local delivery platform, our mission is to deliver an amazing experience—fast, easy, and to your door. ### **Job Description**


**Job Ref ID: JR0082142**

**YOUR WORK\-LIFE OPPORTUNITY:**


Join our team and become an integral part of Glovo's Global Logistics! We provide a dynamic and challenging environment filled with numerous opportunities for growth and development.

  

In this role, you will be responsible for redesigning, testing, and implementing the payment structures that motivate and reward our riders worldwide. By blending deep data analysis and data modeling with creative problem\-solving, your work will ensure our logistics network is efficient, scalable, and fair for our riders. The KPIs you will influence are crucial to operations, as every decision made will directly affect the whole operational investment (biggest company cost).

 **BE A PART OF A TEAM WHERE YOU WILL:**

* Explore and find the most optimal logistics payment structure in order to maximize global riders engagement.
* Strategically redesign our courier payment framework to improve key operational metrics, designing models that reward factors like vehicle used, distance, weight, and peak\-hour availability.
* Dive deep into massive datasets to identify trends, drivers, and opportunities. Your insights will be the foundation for optimizing our entire operational investment.
* Own the experimentation process to validate your ideas. You will design, run, and analyze experiments (A/B testing, switchback tests) to precisely measure the impact of payment structure changes before a global rollout.
* Continuously monitor the performance of your strategies. You will track KPIs, assess the effectiveness of your changes, and make data\-driven adjustments as needed.
* Understand and address local and regional needs by stepping into the shoes of the riders and truly understanding their perspective.

* Degree in Engineering, Maths or another STEM field.

Si un número te dice tanto como una buena idea, y eres de los resolutivos que no esperan a que se lo pidan… bienvenido/a a la manada.

-------------------


Todo el mundo cuenta la historia bonita de startup. La nuestra no es esa.


Somos Ucademy: empezamos en 2022, cuando Ramiro y Pablo volvieron de Bali con una idea y ni un euro de inversión externa. * **Carlota Fernández** (Brand Specialist)
* **Michelangelo Iossa** (Social Ads Specialist)
* **Marta Varela** (Marketing Specialist)

-------------


Serás el puente entre el reporting diario, la optimización táctica de campañas, y la producción creativa junto a Brand. Vigilarás de cerca cómo van las campañas, detectarás desviaciones antes de que sean un problema, ajustarás lo que haga falta ajustar, y ayudarás a que las nuevas creatividades salgan a tiempo.


Aquí vas a aprender haciendo, no observando.

Revisarás a diario las métricas de las campañas activas en Meta, TikTok y Google (spend, CPL, CAC, CTR). Actualizarás dashboards y reportes de seguimiento. Detectarás pronto cualquier desviación y la escalarás al responsable de Paid.

**️ Optimización de campañas** — Pasar de "veo un problema" a "lo soluciono".  

Harás ajustes tácticos sobre campañas en curso: pausar o escalar anuncios según rendimiento, rotar creatividades fatigadas, revisar segmentaciones y pujas. Aplicarás lo aprendido en el reporting diario para mantener el CAC dentro de objetivo.

**Colaboración con Brand**

Apoyarás en el diseño de piezas (estáticas y vídeo) y en la redacción de guiones y copies. Ayudarás a preparar los creativos para su lanzamiento en cada plataforma.

* Te integras en la operativa diaria de Paid.
* Reportas de manera autónoma sobre las campañas.
* Entregas y activas tu primera pieza creativa en campaña.


Objetivo: demostrar que dominas las métricas clave, conoces las plataformas y aportas valor desde ya, aunque con supervisión.

* Gestionas el reporting y la optimización táctica sin depender de otros.
* Eres proactivo/a en el sprint de creatividades.
* Solo necesitas supervisión en decisiones de mayor impacto.


Objetivo: que dejes de necesitar que te digan qué hacer cada día.

**90 días — parte de la manada**

* Tomas decisiones de optimización de campañas sin supervisión directa.


Objetivo: ser una pieza fiable del sistema de Paid.

**Qué buscamos en ti**

* Experiencia, aunque sea inicial o de prácticas, gestionando o dando soporte en campañas de Ads (Meta, TikTok y/o Google).
* Nociones de diseño gráfico y manejo de al menos una herramienta (Canva, Photoshop, Illustrator o Figma).

**El animal que buscamos**

title: Excellence & Execution Head

### **Summary**

The Execution Excellence Head leads the enterprise\-wide evolution of execution standards across the product lifecycle, from two years pre\-launch through loss of exclusivity. * Field Excellence
* Integrated Insights
* Data, Analytics \& Platforms (DAP)
* Capability Building
* Customer Excellence

* Drive standardization of tools, processes, and data governance frameworks.
* Enable adoption of AI\-powered solutions and advanced analytics platforms.
* Manage business readiness and deployment of global execution excellence initiatives and technology platforms.
* Foster digital, technology, and AI capability development across the organization.

### **Capability Building**

* Build and deploy world\-class capabilities across Marketing, Sales, Medical Affairs, and Value \& Access.
* Assess future capability requirements based on strategic priorities and evolving industry trends.
* Deliver impactful learning journeys, curricula, and development programs.
* Establish standards for learning governance, effectiveness measurement, and capability outcomes.
* Partner with global teams and external vendors to deliver innovative learning experiences.

### **Customer Excellence**

* Drive integrated customer engagement excellence across Commercial and Value \& Access organizations.
* Lead omnichannel strategy activation and customer journey optimization.
* Ensure launch readiness through robust planning, orchestration, execution, and continuous improvement processes.
* Optimize content deployment, customer engagement strategies, and promotional excellence frameworks.
* Coordinate congresses, strategic events, and customer engagement initiatives.
* Drive implementation of global frameworks including ICE, IpEx, and launch excellence programs.

### **Leadership \& Culture**

* Lead, inspire, and develop a diverse team of execution excellence professionals.
* Foster a high\-performance culture focused on accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Build strong succession pipelines and future leadership capabilities.
* Drive transformation through Novartis Leadership Expectations and a growth mindset culture.
* Role model the highest standards of ethics, integrity, compliance, and patient focus.

**Essential Requirements**
--------------------------

### **Education**

* University degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Biosciences, or a related field.
* Advanced degree preferred.

### **Experience**

* Extensive leadership experience (typically 12\+ years) within the pharmaceutical industry, consulting, FMCG, or related sectors.
* Proven track record leading commercial organizations, business transformation, or execution excellence functions.
* Experience working across multiple execution excellence capabilities such as analytics, field operations, customer excellence, digital transformation, capability building, or market insights.
* Demonstrated success leading complex change initiatives and influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority.
* Experience operating in highly matrixed, cross\-functional environments.

### **Skills \& Expertise**

* Strong business acumen with deep understanding of the pharmaceutical product lifecycle from pre\-launch through loss of exclusivity.
* Advanced strategic thinking, analytical, forecasting, and insight\-generation capabilities.
* Expertise in digital transformation, technology adoption, AI enablement, and data\-driven decision\-making.

title: Senior Direct Response Funnel Copywriter & Strategist
description:
About Us


HarZa Group is a fast\-growing operator of direct\-to\-consumer brands in health and wellness. Our flagship brand, Rejuvacare, serves more than 400,000 customers with products targeting chronic pain and mobility, including RejuvaKnee, FootRenew, RejuvaFlow and OzemPatch. We ship primarily to the United States and run a membership program that powers recurring revenue. The company has scaled 12x in a single year to nearly 150 people across more than 15 countries. We are remote\-first, async\-first, and hold a high standard of accountability across everything we do.


The Role


We are looking for an exceptional senior direct response copywriter to take ownership of our post\-click funnels. This is not a role for someone who receives a brief, writes the copy and moves on. We are looking for someone who treats funnels the way an exceptional creative strategist treats advertising: research the customer and the market, form a hypothesis, develop the concept, write the copy, get the funnel launched, study the performance, identify the constraint, develop the next test, and turn every result into a feedback loop.


You will be deeply involved in the commercial performance of everything you write. Once a funnel goes live you should be watching click\-through rates, advertorial to sales page click\-through, quiz completion, sales page and checkout conversion, revenue per visitor, average order value, order bump and upsell take rates, refund rates and contribution margin. A page is not finished when the copy is approved. It is finished when it has launched, been measured, and produced a learning that improves the next page.


Your ultimate objective is to remove the founders from writing and reviewing routine funnel copy. Initially they will remain closely involved and may still write a large share of it. You will work directly with them, learn their frameworks, understand their decision\-making, and gradually take ownership of the function. Success means reaching the point where the founders no longer need to write funnel copy, rewrite your work, or independently double\-check it before launch. From there you create leverage through AI systems, documented processes and, in time, additional writers trained and managed beneath you.


A Note on the Category


This is claims\-led direct response, not product\-led ecommerce, and the distinction matters more than any other line in this description. Our products address chronic pain and mobility. The benefit is not visually obvious, it cannot be demonstrated in a photograph, and it cannot be sold on aspiration. Belief has to be built through mechanism, proof, advertorial and presell structure, and honest handling of objections, all inside the compliance limits of a health category.


Copywriters who have scaled fashion, accessories, beauty or other visually self\-evident products often find that their playbook does not transfer. A strong track record in a product\-led category is welcome but does not substitute for this. We will prioritize candidates who have written for health, wellness, supplements or another claims\-sensitive category and who understand what can and cannot be said.


Why This Role Is Different


The founders have generated more than nine figures in post\-purchase upsell revenue in under twenty\-four months. That figure is post\-purchase upsell revenue specifically, not total front\-end company revenue. You will get direct access to the frameworks behind those results, existing research, templates, processes and funnel data, direct feedback and training from the founders, a portfolio of brands and offers with significant traffic, a high\-volume testing environment where your ideas get launched and measured, and real commercial data across multiple funnel types, offers and traffic sources.


This is an opportunity to develop beyond being a copywriter. The right person can progress toward Head of Funnel Copy, Head of Funnel Strategy, Director of Conversion, or operator of one of our portfolio brands. We prefer to promote from within, and progression is based on commercial results, leadership ability and the amount of responsibility you can absorb.

 **Requirements**  

What You Will Own


Post\-Click Funnel Strategy


Act as the strategic owner of post\-click messaging and conversion copy. Participate in marketing, campaign and offer planning, understand what each traffic source needs after the click, and ensure message continuity between the advertisement, presell page, sales page, checkout and upsell journey. Recommend the right funnel format based on the offer, traffic source, customer awareness and market sophistication, and determine when a campaign needs an advertorial, listicle, quiz, long\-form page, short\-form page or another structure. Collaborate with media buyers and creative strategists to understand the promise that generated the click, and identify disconnects between the ad message and the landing page experience. Your remit begins at the click, but you must understand the whole acquisition system to make intelligent post\-click decisions.


Customer and Market Research


Research the customer before developing the copy. Analyze reviews, surveys, support tickets, customer interviews, call transcripts, refund reasons and community discussions. Study competitor offers, positioning, mechanisms, pricing and funnel structures. Identify desires, fears, frustrations, failed solutions, objections and buying triggers, understand the customer's level of awareness and the sophistication of the market, and distinguish between what customers say they want and what their behaviour suggests they value. Build voice\-of\-customer libraries that preserve the language customers actually use, validate that claims are supportable and appropriate for the category, and convert raw research into usable copy insight rather than research documents nobody reads.


Hypothesis Before Writing


Every meaningful funnel project begins with a clear hypothesis. Identify the metric or funnel stage being targeted, diagnose the likely reason for underperformance, state the customer insight behind the diagnosis, define what will change and why it should influence behaviour, select a primary success metric and the guardrails around it, and determine what result would validate or invalidate the idea. The first question is not what copy should I write. It is what is the constraint, why does it exist, and what evidence suggests this is the right solution.


Writing Complete Funnels


Write and optimize new offer positioning, unique mechanisms, big ideas, hooks and leads, advertorials, listicles, quiz flows, long\-form and short\-form sales pages, product detail pages, offer sections, pricing and bundle presentation, guarantees, checkout copy, order bumps, post\-purchase upsells, downsells, cross\-sells, funnel transitions, calls to action, and the supporting briefs for page graphics and visual proof. You must be able to develop a major long\-form funnel from a blank page and equally to identify and rewrite the one critical section inside an existing funnel.


The Offer, Not Only the Words


Copy cannot be separated from the offer. You will think critically about positioning, price, quantity, bundles, discounts, bonuses, guarantees, payment options, shipping thresholds, subscription structures, order bumps, upsell sequencing and offer continuity through the funnel. You should be willing to conclude that the copy is not the main problem and that the right recommendation is to change the offer, reorder the upsells, change the price, improve the guarantee, remove a step or target a different segment. Your responsibility is to improve the commercial result, not to defend the original brief.


Funnel Economics


Understand the underlying economics of each offer, including selling price, cost of goods, pick and pack, shipping, payment processing, discounts, refunds, chargebacks, subscription take rates, upsell margins, gross and contribution margin, customer acquisition cost, and revenue and profit per visitor. A higher AOV is not automatically better if contribution margin falls, a higher conversion rate is not better if refunds rise, and a pricing test must be judged on full funnel economics rather than one isolated metric. You do not need to be a finance professional. You do need to think like an owner.


Staying Close to Live Performance


Once your copy is launched, confirm the correct version went live, review performance against the control and at each funnel step, segment where appropriate, compare mobile and desktop, look for discrepancies between traffic sources, use heatmaps and behavioural data where helpful, and compare primary against guardrail metrics. Document what worked, what did not and why, recommend the next action, and feed every meaningful learning back into research and writing. You should feel personal ownership of the result without becoming defensive when an idea loses. A losing test that produces a real learning is useful. A test launched without a hypothesis and never reviewed is not.


The Learning System and AI Leverage


Build and maintain a searchable archive of tests and results recording the original problem, hypothesis, change, result and learning. Identify recurring patterns across brands and funnel types, separate genuine principles from conclusions drawn on insufficient data, convert repeated winners into reusable frameworks, and prevent failed concepts from being unknowingly repeated. Insight should become company knowledge rather than living in one person's head.


Alongside that, become highly AI\-enabled. Use and improve AI\-assisted systems for research synthesis, voice\-of\-customer clustering, transcript and review analysis, competitor and mechanism research, angle development, hypothesis generation, copy outlining, first drafts, variations, objection identification, quality control, claim consistency review, funnel analysis and test documentation. You will not use a generic chatbot to produce first drafts. You will help build structured processes containing the right context, approved source material, brand knowledge, customer research, historical winners, founder frameworks, defined quality criteria and clear review stages. The standard is not whether AI was used. It is whether AI helped us produce better research, better copy, more tests and faster learning without lowering quality.


What We Are Looking For


Substantial professional experience in direct response copywriting, gained over several years writing for real offers with meaningful traffic. A portfolio containing both long\-form and short\-form funnel copy, significant experience writing for cold traffic, and proven experience in DTC ecommerce, direct response or another measurable\-response environment. Evidence that your work has generated meaningful revenue or measurable conversion improvement. Experience writing complete funnels rather than isolated page sections, including advertorials, listicles, sales pages, quizzes, checkouts and post\-purchase upsells.


Experience in health, wellness, supplements or another claims\-sensitive category, and an understanding of how to build belief where the benefit is not visually demonstrable. A strong grasp of customer awareness, market sophistication, offers, mechanisms, leads, proof, objections and risk reversal. The ability to conduct and synthesize deep customer research and turn it into a clear hypothesis and a persuasive argument.


Strong analytical fluency and comfort with funnel performance data, the ability to diagnose where a funnel is losing customers, a working understanding of AOV, revenue per visitor, upsell take rates, gross margin and contribution margin, experience creating and evaluating conversion tests, and the ability to distinguish correlation, noise and meaningful evidence.


Strong AI fluency with evidence of using AI inside a real research, writing or analysis workflow. The ability to write quickly without sacrificing strategic depth, the confidence to challenge a weak brief or assumption, the humility to change direction when the data disproves an idea, the communication skills to work with founders, media buyers, designers and analysts, and the potential to train and lead additional writers as the function grows. You must be able to overlap consistently with our collaboration window of 8:00am to 12:00pm EST.


High\-volume Meta, native, Google or affiliate traffic, post\-purchase upsell funnels, portfolio or multi\-brand environments, CRO or direct response agencies, subscription offers, and experience building copy systems or training programs are all highly advantageous.


Evidence We Expect to See


Applicants should demonstrate results, not simply submit polished writing samples. Strong evidence includes funnel revenue, conversion rate improvements, revenue per visitor and AOV improvements, upsell take rate and contribution margin improvements, results against an established control, evidence of scaling an offer, before and after funnel performance, and a sequence of tests showing how an insight developed over time.


We understand that candidates may be under confidentiality agreements. Results can be anonymized, but you should still be able to explain what the offer was, what the original problem was, what you personally owned, what research you conducted, what hypothesis you formed, what you changed, which metric moved, how much traffic supported the conclusion, and what happened next. We are more interested in clear thinking and honest attribution than impressive numbers without context.


This Role Is Not


This is not a junior copywriting position, a brand copy role, a content or social media role, or an ad\-copy\-only position. It is not a role where you write from a brief without questioning it, where your responsibility ends when the document is submitted, or where you would rather your work was not measured. It is not a pure CRO analyst role in which you never write, nor a management\-only role in which you no longer produce. It is not for someone who uses AI to generate generic copy and calls that leverage, who needs the founders to supply every angle and mechanism, who waits to be told which test to run, or who blames media buying, design or development without investigating the full funnel.

 **Benefits**  

What We Offer


A fully remote senior position with genuine ownership of a function that directly determines how fast the business can move. We offer paid time off, a monthly wellness stipend, medical insurance support, a company\-funded computer allowance after a tenure milestone, a birthday gift card, an in\-country meetup allowance, and participation in company\-funded leadership offsites. You will have direct access to the founders, a high\-volume testing environment, and the mandate to build the system rather than inherit someone else's process.

title: Head of Web Production (DTC Growth Technology)
description:
About Us


HarZa Group is a fast\-growing operator of direct\-to\-consumer brands in health and wellness. Our flagship brand, Rejuvacare, serves more than 400,000 customers with products targeting chronic pain and mobility, including RejuvaKnee, FootRenew, RejuvaFlow and OzemPatch. We ship primarily to the United States and run a membership program that powers recurring revenue. The company has scaled 12x in a single year to nearly 150 people across more than 15 countries. We are remote\-first, async\-first, and hold a high standard of accountability across everything we do.


The Role


We are a direct\-to\-consumer business where technology is a direct function of marketing. Our marketing team can develop a campaign idea and write the copy for it in a single day, but that idea only starts producing revenue once it has become a live, accurate and fully functioning landing page, checkout or funnel. The speed of our production function therefore sets the speed of the entire business.


We are hiring a Head of Web Production to build and own the operating system through which marketing requirements become live digital experiences. Your responsibility is not to manage tasks, chase deadlines or add project management meetings. It is to redesign how the work gets done. You will examine every stage of production, remove unnecessary handoffs, improve requirements, manage dependencies, install effective quality controls, and decide where AI, automation, page builders, reusable components or traditional development should be used.


For every requirement you should be asking whether this genuinely needs a developer, whether it can be built from an existing component or template, whether an AI\-enabled page builder can complete most of it, whether the marketing team can safely complete it without engineering, whether the requirement can be eliminated or standardized, whether the quality check can be automated, and why it is taking as long as it is. Your job is to protect the business objective while continuously challenging the method used to achieve it.


To be explicit about scope, this is not a cloud infrastructure or site reliability role. This is web production and development operations for a high\-volume direct response marketing business.

 **Requirements**  

What You Will Own


The Production Operating System


Map and redesign the workflow from marketing request to production launch, identifying bottlenecks, unnecessary handoffs, waiting time and duplicated work, and establishing clear ownership at every stage. Define what information must exist before work can begin, create work\-in\-progress limits and prioritization rules, and build separate production lanes for urgent changes, standard pages, experiments and complex technical projects so that urgent work stops destroying the predictability of planned work. Create clear escalation paths for blockers and for requirements that change mid\-build.


Requirements and Task Definition


Build standardized briefs for landing pages, checkouts, funnels, upsells and technical changes, and establish a Definition of Ready for every category of work so that incomplete or ambiguous requests never enter development. Ensure every requirement carries complete copy, design direction, references, responsive behaviour, tracking requirements and acceptance criteria, and translate marketing intent into specifications that developers and page builders can execute without repeated clarification. Create a controlled process for requirements that change after development has begun.


AI\-First Production


Audit the full production process for opportunities to use AI and automation, evaluate AI coding tools, AI page builders, no\-code platforms, reusable components and template\-based systems, and determine the right balance between developers, page builders, designers and AI\-enabled operators. Build workflows where AI converts approved briefs, copy and designs into high\-quality first drafts, install guardrails that allow non\-developers to build safely without damaging performance, tracking or brand standards, and reduce repetitive development through reusable sections and approved design systems. Measure the actual impact of AI on cycle time, cost, quality and throughput rather than assuming it.


Dependencies and Capacity


Create visibility over the workload and capacity of development, design and other shared resources, identify dependencies before work enters production, and sequence work based on when copy, graphics, video, development and approvals will realistically be available. Prevent developers from being assigned work that cannot be completed because a dependency is missing, build a capacity planning system that lets marketing understand what can actually be delivered and when, and surface constraints early enough for the business to reprioritize or find an alternative. Reduce reliance on informal messages and on individual managers holding critical information in their heads.


Quality Built Into the Process


Move quality control upstream instead of relying on final\-stage inspection. Introduce developer self\-QC before any task is submitted, create standardized QC checklists by page and funnel type, define acceptance criteria before development begins, and establish an independent final QC process that does not depend entirely on one person. Implement automated testing wherever practical, including visual regression, broken links, responsive layouts, tracking, checkout functionality, browser compatibility and page performance. Categorize defects, track root causes, and ensure repeated defects change the underlying system, checklist, component or training rather than being corrected one at a time.


Team Structure and Capability


Lead the existing production team and raise its operating standard. Determine which work should be completed by developers and which should be completed by AI\-enabled production specialists, and make sure capability is matched to the work. Coach the team on estimation, task clarification, self\-QC and AI\-assisted workflows, set clear performance expectations for speed, predictability and quality, and build enough documentation and shared visibility that the function does not depend on any single person holding critical context.


The Measurement System


Build and maintain reporting on request\-to\-launch cycle time, active production time versus waiting time, throughput by work category, on\-time delivery, clarification interactions after assignment, first\-pass QC rate, average revision rounds, escaped defect rate, rework hours, blocker age, the share of work completed through reusable components or AI\-assisted workflows, cost per page or funnel, and marketing launch delays caused by technology or creative dependencies. These metrics exist to improve the system, not to generate reporting.


How Success Will Be Measured


Your first thirty days are about establishing a baseline. We do not currently measure cycle time, waiting time, clarification loops, rework or escaped defects, so your first task is to map the current state from request to launch and put real numbers against it, then produce a prioritized roadmap for improving the system. We would rather agree ambitious targets against real data than hand you numbers invented before anyone measured anything.


By sixty days we expect a standardized intake and requirements process, clear Definitions of Ready and Done, service\-level expectations by category of work, visibility over development and creative capacity, dependency planning across copy, design, video, development, tracking and approvals, piloted AI\-assisted and template\-driven workflows, and a live operating dashboard covering speed, quality and throughput.


By ninety days we expect the function to be trending strongly toward a materially shorter median request\-to\-launch cycle time, the large majority of work delivered by the committed date, the large majority of work passing final QC without another development round, a sharp reduction in issues identified after approval by the CEO or the media buyer, full visibility over active work, dependencies, blockers and capacity, standard page types produced without bespoke development, and higher throughput without a corresponding increase in headcount. Exact targets will be finalized against your baseline.  

  

What We Are Looking For


Significant experience improving the operations of a web development, digital production or growth technology team, with a proven record of reducing delivery time, increasing throughput or improving first\-pass quality. Experience in an environment where development speed directly affects revenue. A strong working understanding of landing pages, ecommerce funnels, checkouts, upsells, testing and conversion\-focused web production.


Enough technical depth to challenge estimates, architecture choices and development approaches, including a working understanding of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, APIs, analytics, tracking, page builders and modern web development workflows. Experience implementing AI tools or automation inside a real production environment rather than as a pilot or a talking point. Experience designing intake processes, acceptance criteria, capacity planning and quality control systems, and a strong grasp of dependencies and constraint management.


The ability to communicate effectively with marketers, copywriters, designers, media buyers and developers, and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders when a requirement is unclear, unnecessarily complicated or being solved in the wrong way. Strong analytical ability, comfort making decisions from operational data, and a bias toward simplification, standardization and measurable results.


Experience with direct response ecommerce, high\-volume web production, Shopify, Checkout Champ, Figma, landing page builders, CRO testing and marketing analytics is highly advantageous. Formal qualifications are not required where there is strong evidence of relevant outcomes. You must be able to overlap consistently with our collaboration window of 8:00am to 12:00pm EST.


This Role Is Not


This is not a traditional cloud\-infrastructure DevOps role, a Jira administration role, a project coordinator position, or a role focused on running agile ceremonies. It is not a role for someone who accepts every requirement without questioning it, whose first answer to any constraint is additional headcount, who can describe AI tools but has never embedded them into an operational workflow, or who wants engineering leadership disconnected from marketing and revenue.

 **Benefits**  

What We Offer


A fully remote senior position with genuine ownership of a function that directly determines how fast the business can move. We offer paid time off, a monthly wellness stipend, medical insurance support, a company\-funded computer allowance after a tenure milestone, a birthday gift card, an in\-country meetup allowance, and participation in company\-funded leadership offsites. You will have direct access to the founders, a high\-volume testing environment, and the mandate to build the system rather than inherit someone else's process.

description:
**Contracting unit:** \- Office of the Chief Scientist, CGIAR System Organisation


**Budget Ceiling: \-** USD 30,000 (all\-inclusive; competitive open call)

**Duration: \-** 6–8 weeks

**2027 milestone: \-** Blueprint endorsed; build procurement decision made

**Delivery lead: \-** Portfolio Performance and Results Team (PPT)

**Oversight: \-** Steering Group (Office of the Chief Scientist, DTA, Digital)

**Deadline for Applications: \-** 8 September 2026, 23:59hrs (Paris time GMT\+2\)




**Background**


The Performance \& Results Management System (PRMS) is CGIAR's core infrastructure for portfolio planning, results reporting, quality assurance, adaptive management, risk management and accountability. It was identified in the CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework as a common system housing planning, theory of change management, stage\-gate decision points, and annual reporting — with linked datasets, an integrated dashboard for funders and management, and access aligned to international standards. A February 2021 Accenture fit\-for\-purpose assessment translated this into implementation requirements: integrated business applications, standardized data definitions across CGIAR systems, and comprehensive onboarding of end users. CGIAR invested approximately USD 800k per year to build and run that system during the period 2022\-25, with joint Independent Advisory and Internal Audit review during rollout to ensure delivery against specification.


The PRMS was built for a context of relatively stable institutional requirements: a defined set of manual inputs, largely from Window 1/2 funding, processed sequentially — each stage waiting for the previous — to produce a predetermined set of outputs on a predictable cycle. Bespoke requests that fell outside those predetermined outputs required specialists to extract value case by case. That design was rational for the conditions in which it was built. Five shifts prompt a redesign.


The first is the nature of demand. The portfolio now requires dynamic, on\-demand, user\-defined outputs — some anticipated, many not. New business requirements arrive at unpredictable intervals: a GST decision requiring real\-time performance data for resource allocation, a donor wanting a bespoke cut across Programs, an AI tool needing to interrogate the data layer directly. A system with predetermined outputs cannot serve this.


The second is the scope of what the system must hold. Window 3/bilateral funding — around 1000 non\-pooled projects — is heterogeneous in structure, language, and reporting logic. W3/bilateral data cannot be pre\-programmed into the system; it is a different problem type, and the current architecture has no way to accommodate it.


The third is the ability to orchestrate. CGIAR now deploys operational AI tools — for example SNAP, the zero\-draft generator, the QA helper, the Progress Tracking Solution — that need to query, submit to, and coordinate across the system. The current PRMS is not orchestrable: its components are not designed to be called, sequenced, or managed by an AI agent. A system that AI can understand and act on any layer is a key requirement.


The fourth is the multiplicity of data sources the system must draw on. Portfolio evidence already sits across many instruments and repositories — among them legacy CRP and Initiative results, current Program and Accelerator results, Plans of Results and Budget (PoRB), Projected Benefits, the Impact Compendium, CGSpace, AnaPlan and others — each with its own structure and logic, with limited interconnections.


The fifth is the technological revolution in data management. The maturing of AI and large language models has changed what is possible: data no longer has to be captured through fixed forms and rigid fields to be usable, and outputs no longer have to be predetermined and assembled by hand. This reframes the redesign itself — not a faster version of the old model, but a shift to more flexible, AI\-native handling of data that cuts duplication, lowers effort, and can generate higher\-quality outputs on demand while maintaining core security safeguards.


The new PRMS must be modular, reconfigurable, and interoperable by design — not simply cheaper to build, but cheaper to run and extend, with a clear view of the trade\-off between reduced human effort and the real costs of AI\-driven processing at scale.


Two developments in 2026 show what this looks like in practice. The CGIAR Progress Tracking Solution — launched in July 2026 — demonstrates a possible target architecture: AI\-assisted, modular, with a human validation layer, open enough for users to connect their own systems via API. The June 2026 GST\-endorsed Guidance Note on Program/Accelerator\-level prioritization establishes that actual performance against theories of change will directly inform W1/W2 fund allocation from 2026 onward: PRMS data must be queryable in real time to feed consequential resource allocation decisions, not compiled into static reports after the fact. Together, they define what fit for purpose now requires.


Purpose
This commission produces an architectural blueprint for a rebuilt PRMS — the design basis for a subsequent build investment. It is not a developer\-ready technical specification. It is the front end of a two\-stage process: design now, procure and build against it. Steering Group endorsement of this blueprint will be the decision gate for the larger investment.


The starting point is not the technology but the people the system serves — funders, senior leadership and governing bodies, Program and Accelerator directors, Centers, and external partners — and the outputs they need, from stabilized reports and dashboards to on\-demand answers tailored to a specific question. The design works back from those needs to the data the system already holds, and it must make the system materially lighter to feed — less manual entry, less duplication, less double reporting — not only cheaper to run.


The design target is a system that is orchestrable: modular, reconfigurable, and interoperable, built so that AI agents can understand and operate across any layer — or so that any process can run without AI, depending on the risk appetite and the requirement. A result linked to a causal pathway is the atomic unit; everything else is an expression of it. Report once, use many times. The system must function as a data layer that CGIAR tools and authorised external actors can query, contribute to, and act on — not a system that only produces predetermined outputs for predetermined audiences.


The blueprint must address constraints: that replacing human effort with AI\-driven processing shifts cost rather than eliminates it, and that AI operating costs at scale must be designed for; and that Center and Program adoption has been suboptimal, and the design must address why. Both are in scope. The blueprint must be specific enough to brief the Performance and Results Management Steering Group, scope a build procurement, and hold a development team accountable.


Objectives* Map the demand the system must serve. Identify the priority users and uses — internal and external — and the outputs each needs, from those already mandated by CGIAR governance to the on\-demand, tailored outputs that AI now makes possible. Distinguish what the system already delivers well from what users cannot currently obtain.
* Take stock of the foundational building blocks the portfolio already runs on — for example the Theory of Change, the Projected Benefits model, the Results Framework and its 3 indicator tiers, PoRB/PoD planning instruments — and assess their fitness as the base for a redesigned system rather than starting from a blank slate.
* Characterize the data supply and its fragmentation — what is entered by hand versus captured automatically, and what lives across CGIAR, donor, and Center systems — and consider the growing overlap between monitoring data and science or project data under FAIR. Set out what this implies for a system that draws on existing sources rather than re\-collecting data during each reporting cycle.
* Define the connecting layer between demand and supply — the core of this commission. At the level of principle and direction, set out how a result linked to a causal pathway becomes the atomic unit that is reported once and reused many times; how the layer is made FAIR, API\-first, and orchestrable so that CGIAR tools and authorised external actors — including AI agents — can query and contribute to it; and how heterogeneous W3/bilateral data is accommodated without being forced into a W1/W2 mold.
* Show how the redesign lightens the load — and where it does not. Explain how it may reduce fields, duplication, and double reporting and shift effort from manual data entry toward data interoperability, while being honest about the trade\-offs, including AI operating costs at scale and the points where human judgment must remain.
* Set out the direction of travel and a phased path — what is foundational and should be settled now versus what can be resolved at the build stage, including a costed view of the interim 2027 release and the fuller rebuild. As part of this, diagnose at a strategic level why Centers and Programs have historically, to different extents, routed around PRMS, and what the new system must do differently to earn adoption.


Scope and Constraints
This is a conceptual design commission. The consultant produces the architectural blueprint and roadmap, with the Performance and Results Management Steering Group providing oversight and independent challenge. While security, access controls, audit trails and availability are core aspects of the future system, detailed technical specification — schema definitions, API contracts, and migration mechanics — is deliberately out of scope at this stage: the blueprint establishes direction and principle, and the build phase resolves the detail.


Ready by 2027 means: blueprint endorsed by the Steering Group and a build procurement decision made — not full system deployment. Specific PRMS capabilities needed for the 2027 reporting cycle will be identified in the roadmap and may be delivered as an interim release against the existing system while the rebuild proceeds. The costed build roadmap must give PPT and Centers a concrete transition path for modules currently under active management — including the Planning Module and POD — specifying which planned enhancements should continue during the review period and where enhancement work should pause pending the interim 2027 release, so teams are not left to decide this unilaterally while the review is underway.


W3/bilateral data integration — where permitted by Centers — is within scope. It is a distinct architectural problem that the blueprint must address — not a future phase or an edge case. The heterogeneity of non\-pooled project data, the challenge of connecting it to the CGIAR results hierarchy, and the implications for Center\-level data ownership and access are design questions the consultant must answer.


Center and Program adoption is a governance and change management challenge, not an architectural one. The blueprint will diagnose it and specify design requirements that reduce friction, but the Steering Group — not the consultant — must own the adoption strategy.


Given that PPT leads both delivery and the Steering Group secretariat, the blueprint will be subject to independent technical review by at least two Steering Group members with relevant technical expertise before endorsement. This is a process requirement, not optional.


Deliverables* Architectural blueprint.
* Costed build roadmap.
* Performance and Results Management Steering Group briefing deck.


Methodology* Review of PRMS technical documentation, AI tool dependency evidence, MELIAF Interoperability Framework, March 2026 operational incident record, enhancement request history, and existing API documentation and agent integration work produced by the PRMS infrastructure team.
* Interviews with PRMS infrastructure team, PPT AI tool developers, MELIAF workstream leads, Center MEL leads, and Center representatives who have actively worked around PRMS. The interview set must include demand\-side users, not only the supply side.
* Co\-design sessions with PPT to validate architecture decisions.
* Independent technical review of draft blueprint before finalisation — reviewers nominated by the Performance and Results Management Steering Group.


Timeline
Duration: 6–8 weeks

* Weeks 1–2: Document review, interviews, co\-design sessions
* Weeks 3–5: Blueprint drafting
* Week 6: PPT review and iteration
* Weeks 7–8: Independent technical review, revisions, Steering Group briefing

  

**Requirements**  

  

Required Expertise* Senior\-level expertise in data architecture and API design for complex, federated data environments — including experience designing for AI orchestration and agentic access patterns.
* Advanced understanding of AI/ML pipeline requirements — practical understanding of what LLM\-based and agentic tools require from upstream data infrastructure, including cost modelling at scale.
* Deep experience in MEL and risk\-informed systems in international development — results frameworks, theory of change, indicator management, and bilateral reporting structures.
* Proven ability to advise on organizational change and adoption in federated, multi\-stakeholder settings.
* Track record producing architectural blueprints that non\-technical leadership can act on and developers can build against.
* Strong capacity to translate user, governance, and reporting needs into system and data requirements — a service\-design sensibility that starts from what users must be able to answer.
* Experience with CGIAR, multilateral research organisations, or comparable federated institutional environments is an advantage.

**Required application documents**

* A **technical proposal**, including:
* Updated CVs and a cover letter explaining how the consultant’s qualifications and experience meet the requirements of the assignment;
* A short approach to the work, maximum 2–4 pages, outlining how the consultant proposes to address the objectives and deliverables in these TORs, with reference to comparable assignments that demonstrate the required expertise.
* A **financial proposal in USD**, quoted as a lump sum and supported by a cost breakdown by level of effort per deliverable. Combine both technical and financial proposal in one document.

**Evaluation and communication**


CGIAR places strong emphasis on ensuring that the objectives of the PRMS Architectural Redesign Blueprint are met. Proposals will be assessed on technical merit and value for money. Only pre\-selected candidates will be contacted.


Annex 1: CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework’s definition of the**Performance and Results Management System (December 2020\)**


Building on investments made in the current phase of CGIAR research programming, a comprehensive, mature and accessible Performance \& Results Management System (PRMS) that encompasses planning, monitoring, and reporting will provide robust information upon which to take informed decisions. It will provide:

* Practical services aligned to meet learning, accountability and resource mobilization objectives,
* Dashboards open to Funders and partners, with access to the full set of underlying quality\-checked data, including communications\-focused products capturing collated evidence of CGIAR contribution to change (e.g. outcome/impact case reports).
* Alignment with international standards such as IATI (International Aid Transparency Initiative).


Key PRMS features
The CGIAR PRMS will feature:

* A common system housing plan of work and budget, theory of change management, stage\-gate decision points, and annual reporting processes. It will allow real\-time data collection and day\-to\-day portfolio and Initiative management.
* Key data sets (results, plan of work and budget, grant, finance, stage\-gate specific e.g. Scaling Readiness) will be increasingly linked, for example through CLARISA: CGIAR Level Agricultural Results Interoperable System Architecture, a web service that harmonizes data from across the CGIAR).
* Interface and exchange with big data and partner data sets (e.g. WIPO Green and the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture) will increase. CGIAR will publish relevant data through IATI. CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework 2022\-2030 CGIAR System Organization Page 16 of 20
* CGIAR’s digital knowledge base will make better use of linked data through Knowledge Graphs, and


will use the SDG Interface Ontology to better link its contribution to impact with that of partners.

* An integrated dashboard will draw from relevant data sets to provide transparent data and insights on


CGIAR geographic and thematic presence, contribution to change, spend and partner network.


Users
Target users of the PRMS include CGIAR staff for day\-to\-day Initiative management and reporting, portfolio management and resource mobilization, and Funders and partners to access evidence of CGIAR thematic and geographic presence and progress against stated objectives such as the SDGs.


Security, hosting, maintenance and support
The PRMS will incorporate:

* Secured infrastructure,
* Cloud hosting,
* CGIAR Active Directory integration for user provisioning and account management,
* Access control through Multi\-Factor Authentication,
* Single Sign On,
* Tiered support and maintenance approach aligned with CGIAR’s IT support model.

 **Benefits**

Quiénes somos

We are TK Airport Solutions, a business unit of TKE Group.


TK Elevator (TKE) is a global leader in vertical transportation and urban mobility, providing engineering — from design through installation, maintenance and modernization — for elevators, escalators, moving walkways, passenger boarding bridges, stairlifts, platform lifts and home elevators. TKE employs more than 50\.000 people around the world, being present in more than 100 countries.

  

From our engineering and manufacturing site in Mieres, Asturias, TKAS offers a full portfolio of airport apron and gate mobility solutions. Our **passenger boarding bridges** connect terminals to aircraft safely and efficiently. Our **ground support equipment** covers preconditioned air, ground power units and potable water units for aircraft turnaround. Our **advanced visual docking guidance systems (A\-VDGS)**, including the LiDAR\-based Apron Vision, ensure precise and safe aircraft docking. Our **digital solutions** — MAX Automate, MAX Monitor \& Control and MAX Maintenance Manager — bring AI and remote operation to the apron.


We also provide **modernization and service** programs, including upgrades and spare parts that extend equipment life and performance, and we adapt this same engineering expertise to **seaports**, with our Seaport Passenger Boarding Bridges (SPBB) for ferry and cruise terminals.


Our equipment is used at more than 370 airports in over 100 countries, and TK Elevator boarding bridges have carried over 1\.8 billion passengers worldwide.

description:
**About Safeguard Global:** We enable global expansion without the risk.


Safeguard Global has been at the forefront of global workforce enablement since we pioneered centralised global payments in 2008 and launched the employer of record (EOR) category globally in 2010\. And we haven't stopped there.


Today, with our 500\+ in\-country HR experts, cutting\-edge technology, and comprehensive solutions, we've helped over 2,000 organisations hire, recruit, pay, and manage employees in 170\+ countries.


Because we created this category, we've learned that successful global expansion isn't driven by technology alone. It requires deep global expertise. We call this the marriage of expert and technology, human when it matters.


This means we have the people and the technology to ensure 100% compliance with local, regional, national, and international laws. Together, this ethos and our solutions portfolio allow businesses to scale up or down wherever, however, and whenever they want to expand, without the risk.


**Overview of the role**

We're looking for a **Head of Product, Core Journeys** to lead the platform experience across our core client journey, from hiring a worker through to invoicing for them.


The role is accountable for the platform experience, delivery, and outcome achievement across the core transactional workflows . You'll translate that target experience, combined with the product strategies set by the Directors of Product into a prioritised order of work ; lead ing the product managers who deliver it and ensuring we deliver on business and customer experience objectives.


**What you will be responsible for**

**Platform experience**

* Own the end\-to\-end platform experience across the core client journey, including the transitions between one part of the platform and the next
* Identify where the experience is failing clients and set the plan to correct it
* Own regulatory and compliance obligations as product requirements within your area, working with legal, tax, and the in\-country teams so that they are designed in rather than retrofitted
**Prioritisation and roadmap**

* Translate the platform strategy and commercial priorities into a prioritised order of work for your area
* Feed that prioritisation into the single prioritised roadmap owned by the SVP, Product
* Recommend what is built, what is deferred, and what is retired within your area, and secure agreement with the SVP, Product and the Directors of Product
* Build the case for significant investment, including the value expected, the payback, and the trade\-off against the alternatives
* Work with the Directors of Product to sequence commercial priorities in a way the platform can deliver
**Delivery**

* Hold accountability for delivery against commitment, on time and to the quality bar set in the definition of done
* Work hand in hand with engineering and design leadership, from the earliest shaping of an idea through to release, so that trade\-offs between client need, technical feasibility, and cost are made together
* Work with sales, marketing, customer success, finance, and legal so that what we build is understood, sellable, supportable, and compliant on the day it launches
* Identify and resolve delivery risk early, including teams that are blocked, unclear, or behind
* Manage dependencies within your area and into the connected experience areas
**Customer insight and product performance**

* Build the relationships, with clients and with internal teams, that sustain a continuous understanding of customer and internal pain points, and of the opportunities they point to
* Ground product decisions in client insight, usage data, and market evidence
* Raise the standard of discovery and validation across your teams
* Define the expected outcome for each investment and own the value delivered against it
* Own platform NPS and adoption for the core journey, and act on the results
* Act as the product expert in senior client and prospect conversations, and represent the platform externally where it helps us win and keep clients
**Team leadership**

* Line manage the product managers within your area
* Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and address performance issues early
* Work with each product manager to understand their individual development needs, and take a coaching approach to growing their capability
* Drive AI adoption where it creates the best outcome, recognising that it serves some tasks well and others poorly, and help the product team keep pace with how the role of product is rapidly changing
**What will give you an advantage**

* Eight or more years in product, including at least five leading people
* Proven experience leading product managers in a B2B SaaS or platform business, ideally where several teams contribute to a single client experience
* Experience owning a multi\-team product area end to end, with accountability for both delivery and the value delivered
* A record of defining the expected value of an investment up front and evidencing what was realised
* Knowledge of the HR industry is preferred but not critical
* Experience of building products in a regulated environment, where compliance shapes what can be built
* Enough technical depth to hold a credible conversation with engineering leadership on architecture, platform scalability, and data
* A demonstrable record of developing product managers
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple countries and time zones
**Primary performance metrics**

* **Delivery:** commitments delivered on time and to quality
* **Business impact:** value delivered against the outcomes committed at the point of investment
* **Experience:** platform NPS
* **Adoption:** adoption of the core journey, from hiring to invoicing
*Baselines and annual targets are set with the SVP, Product at the start of each financial year.*

**Competencies**

* **Product judgement:** makes clear recommendations on scope, sequencing, and trade\-offs that hold up over time
* **Strategic thinking:** sets a direction for the platform that connects client need, market direction, and commercial goals
* **Systems thinking:** designs the journey around what matters most to the customer, and focuses only on the work that delivers value
* **Delivery leadership:** maintains a predictability and quality bar across multiple teams without becoming a bottleneck
* **Communication:** strong written and verbal communicator at all levels of the organisation, from SLT to team
* **People development:** understands what each individual needs and coaches them to grow
* **Influencing:** aligns commercial, engineering, and design leadership around a single sequence of work without direct authority
* **Commercial judgement:** determines what is worth building next, and evidences the case
**Key personal attributes**

* **Grit and determination:** moves work forward despite obstacles, and does not give up easily
* **Curiosity:** actively seeks out different points of view, customer needs, and the problems worth solving
* **A leader and a doer:** operates strategically while staying close to the detail
* Warm, open, honest, and fun to work with

Safeguard Global is…Global! We help 1500\+ companies hire, manage, and pay employees in 170\+ countries. Join us to meet diverse talent, explore new cultures, and connect with amazing folks from around the globe. ✈️
